findings.title: Embed template has invalid ERB and will not render
findings.body: The header conditional is closed with `<%- end if %>`, which compiles to invalid Ruby (`end if` with no condition) and raises a syntax error when the embed layout renders `best`. Any request that finds an existing topic therefore 500s instead of showing highlights, so the embed iframe never works for topics that have already been imported. It needs to be `<% end %>`.

findings.title: Imported HTML is stored and rendered unsanitized
findings.body: RSS and remote imports create the topic with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true`. `Post#cook` then returns `raw` unchanged, skipping the normal cook/sanitize pipeline, and both the topic page and `embed/best.html.erb` (`raw post.cooked`) emit that HTML. `PollFeed` feeds `CGI.unescapeHTML` of the feed item straight into this path, and `import` also interpolates the source URL into an `<a href='...'>` without escaping. A feed item or fetched page can therefore store script or a broken-out URL (`http://host/'><script>...`) that runs in the forum origin for every visitor.

findings.title: Unauthenticated embed fetch is an SSRF and topic-creation primitive
findings.body: `import_remote` does `open(url).read` with no scheme allowlist, timeout, size limit, or redirect restriction, then publishes the body as a post by `embed_by_username`. `EmbedController#best` will enqueue that fetch for any client that sends `Referer` whose host equals `embeddable_host` (a header the caller sets; it is not a browser-only check) and any `embed_url` on that host. `open-uri` follows redirects, so a redirect on the allowed host makes the app request internal addresses (for example link-local metadata) and can turn the response into a public topic. The same `open` call is also missing `require 'open-uri'`; unless some other file has already loaded it, `Kernel#open` treats the URL as a local path, the retrieve job errors, and the embed stays on the loading page. `TopicRetriever` only calls `Jobs::PollFeed` (which does require `open-uri`) when feed polling is enabled, so the HTTP fallback is the path that breaks.

findings.title: Feed poll crashes on typical RSS items and blocks embeds
findings.body: `i.content.scrub` assumes every item has a `content` field and that `String#scrub` exists. Standard RSS 2.0 items only have `description`, so `i.content` is nil and this raises NoMethodError; `scrub` itself is also missing on Ruby 1.9/2.0, which this app still boots. The scheduled job sets `retry: false`, so one bad item aborts the whole import. `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute` synchronously before the HTTP fallback whenever feed polling is enabled, so the same exception also prevents on-demand embed retrieval and leaves the iframe reloading `loading` forever.

findings.title: Resize postMessage uses the full referer as targetOrigin
findings.body: The iframe sends `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')`. `postMessage`'s targetOrigin must be an origin (`scheme://host[:port]`), not the full referring URL. A path or query on the referer means the parent origin does not match, the resize message is dropped (or the call throws), and `embed.js` never updates `#discourse-embed-frame` height, so comments are clipped by `scrolling="no"`. The same interpolation is only HTML-escaped, not JavaScript-escaped, so a referer whose host is the configured embeddable host but whose path contains a quote (Rails 3 does not escape `'`) or a JS line terminator breaks out of the string and runs in the forum origin.

findings.title: Throttle key can stick forever if expire does not run
findings.body: The per-URL throttle does `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and only then `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process dies, the connection drops, or expire fails between those calls, the key is left with no TTL. `retrieved_recently?` then stays true for that embed URL forever (unless the caller is staff and passes `no_throttle`), so the article is never fetched and the embed never leaves the loading state. The set and TTL need to be a single atomic SET with expiry.

findings.title: embed_url is varchar(255) with a unique index
findings.body: `t.string :embed_url` is a 255-character varchar, and the unique index is on that column. Article URLs with query strings routinely exceed 255 characters. `TopicEmbed.create!` then raises, the import transaction rolls back, and that page can never be embedded. Two distinct URLs that share the same first 255 characters also collide on the unique index and one of them fails to import.

findings.title: Disqus import now depends on a live fetch and drops category
findings.body: The task used to create the topic locally from the export. It now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which `open`s `t[:link]` with no rescue. A single dead link, non-HTTP link, or timeout raises and aborts the rest of the threads (the `ensure` only restores the rate limiter and email blacklist). The `-c`/`category` option and the `category_id` passed to `PostCreator` were removed, and `TopicEmbed.import` has no category argument, so every imported thread lands in the default category instead of the one the operator selected.

findings.title: Embed success example cannot pass as written
findings.body: The "topic_id is found" example stubs `TopicView.new` but does not return a topic view (Mocha yields nil). The action then renders `best`, which immediately calls `@topic_view.posts` / `@topic_view.topic`. The shared `after` hook also requires `response.should be_success` and `X-Frame-Options == ALLOWALL`. Even after the `end if` template syntax error is fixed, this example 500s and the new controller spec fails, so it does not lock in the embed response.
